checks.name: Content is in the HTML (JavaScript off)
checks.detail: 109 characters visible with scripts off, of 829 a scripted visitor sees while scrolling; h1 visible
checks.fix: Write the headings, copy and links as plain HTML. Never start content at opacity 0 waiting for a script: add the hidden state from JavaScript (for example a class on <html>), so the page reads without it.

checks.name: Works without WebGL / WebGPU
checks.detail: 1 error(s): Uncaught Error: Error creating WebGL context.; 109 of 109 characters visible
checks.fix: Test for the context before building the scene; on failure leave the poster or CSS fallback in place and skip the scene code (assets/scene-shell.js does this).

checks.name: Reduced motion: the page holds still
checks.detail: 60.5 scene frames/s when idle, 0 element(s) changing place, 0 looping or long CSS animation(s), smooth-scroll off; the picture still changes between two screenshots (fine if that is live data, a clock or a video the person started)
checks.fix: Under prefers-reduced-motion draw single still frames (one per beat), turn off parallax, scrubbing, smooth-scroll and looping CSS animation, and keep short fades only.

checks.name: Little script before first paint
checks.detail: 119 KB of script requested before first paint (budget 170 KB); 131 KB in all
checks.fix: Load the 3D engine with a dynamic import() after first paint (or when the scene is near the viewport). Keep the heading as real text so it paints first.

checks.name: Page weight
checks.detail: 131 KB total (script 119, images 0, 3D assets 0, fonts 0); biggest: 119 KB three.min.js; 12 KB index.html
checks.fix: Budget: first scene under about 1.5 MB on phones and 4 MB on desktop. Compress models (meshopt or Draco) and textures (KTX2 / WebP), cut texture size, lazy-load what is below the fold.

checks.name: Phone: pixel ratio is capped
checks.detail: canvas draws at 2x on a 3x screen, 1.3 megapixels
checks.fix: Cap the pixel ratio at 1.5 on touch screens (2 at most) and lower it when frames get slow. A 3x canvas draws 9 pixels for every CSS pixel.

checks.name: Phone: no sideways scroll
checks.fix: Give the scene host overflow: hidden and min-width: 0; size the canvas from its box, not from the window.

checks.name: Scrolling stays native
checks.detail: a 400px wheel step moved the page 400px; root overflow visible/visible
checks.fix: Never change scroll speed or direction and never replace the scrollbar with a transform. Pin with position: sticky and read the scroll position; let the browser do the scrolling.

checks.name: Scene pauses off screen
checks.detail: the canvas is always on screen (or there is none)
checks.fix: Stop the render loop with an IntersectionObserver when the scene leaves the viewport, and on visibilitychange when the tab is hidden.

checks.name: Ambient motion rests or can be paused
checks.detail: 60 frames/s still being drawn about 7s after load with no input
checks.fix: Anything that moves by itself for more than 5 seconds needs a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2), or should settle and render on demand.

checks.name: Survives a lost graphics context
checks.detail: 0 error(s) after the context was lost; webglcontextlost handler present
checks.fix: Listen for webglcontextlost (preventDefault, stop the loop, show the fallback) and rebuild on webglcontextrestored. Phones drop contexts when memory is tight.

notes: No visibilitychange listener: the scene may keep drawing in a hidden tab.
Frame rate was not measured (headless Chrome draws in software). Test on a mid-range phone, or throttle the CPU 4x in DevTools, and aim for a steady 60 fps.

7 piece(s) of text sit straight on the scene with no surface behind them at 100% scroll (for example "04 · Yours", "Tern, in chalk.", "chalk"). Contrast cannot be measured over a moving image: open that screenshot and check no text crosses the subject; give text a lane, a surface or a scrim.
